relevance_note: Case series of three patients with novel heterozygous TNFAIP3 mutations described individually: "Here we describe three unrelated patients with autoimmune lupus nephritis (LN) phenotypes carrying three novel mutations in the TNFAIP3 gene."
method_note: Read the whole paper and typed every value into a Python build script in my scratch directory (no automatic table transcription); a second script checked that every span occurs verbatim in the paper, that every row has every schema field and that enum values are valid. Tables 1-3 have patients as columns; column headers 'Patient 1', 'Patient 2', 'Patient 3' are labelled P1, P2, P3 (the paper's most frequent form), and spans quote the row label through that patient's cell. Table 4 has patients as rows. Table 1 'No' cells, Table 2 'Present'/'Absent' cells and Table 3 'Negative' were read as explicit words of absence (not symbols); empty cells (P1 dsDNA) and 'ND' cells (P1 CRP/ESR, P3 IgE) are not reported. Common SLE risk alleles in Table 5 were not recorded (risk alleles are out of scope). Relatives: mother of P1 (variant row from Table 1 'Mutation origin | From mother'; recurrent oral ulcers); son of P1 (affected; the text only says 'The mutation co-segregated with disease phenotype in the family (Fig. 2A and B)', so no variant row was created for him); mother of P3 (carrier, asymptomatic); P2's two parents, who tested negative ('neither parent harboured the variant'); the paper does not distinguish them, so they are labelled 'parent of P2' and 'parent of P2 2'. P3's father is mentioned only as part of trio WES ('the proband and both parents') with no result or phenotype, so he has no row. Relatives' variant rows leave zygosity, inheritance, functional evidence and pathogenicity as not reported because the paper states these only for the probands. age_at_diagnosis text gives both Table 1 ages (LN diagnosis; genetic diagnosis); the ISO field gives the genetic diagnosis age. Ages such as 'P2, a 3-year-old girl' were read as age at presentation/diagnosis, so age at last evaluation is not reported for the probands. Mother of P3 'asymptomatic' is recorded as one excluded feature row ('asymptomatic' = symptoms absent); her checklist is left not reported because no checklist feature is named. Interpretive checklist calls: P1 thrombocytopenia (listed among SLE diagnostic features) -> cytopenia (autoimmune) observed; P2 'vasculitic rashes' and son of P1 'Henoch–Schönlein purpura' -> vasculitis observed; P3 'Bilateral knee effusion' -> arthritis or arthralgia observed; P2 'Musculoskeletal | No' and 'Ocular | No' were taken as broader absences that exclude arthritis/arthralgia and ocular inflammation. Elevated IL-6 is recorded for all three patients from the Fig. 4 legend 'Elevated serum cytokine IL-6 levels in the three patients' (group statement naming all three); 'without renal insufficiency' for P2 and P3 comes from the statement about 'the patients' (all three). Temporal changes were not treated as contradictions: P2 had no autoantibodies in the first year and later positive ANA/anti-dsDNA; P2 had elevated leucocytes at onset and leukopenia later; P3 had no fever or proteinuria during follow-up after treatment (recorded in severity_or_detail). Inconsistencies noted in the paper: Table 1's onset row is labelled '(years)' but P2's cell reads '10 month'; the Discussion says P2 and P3 showed marked autoimmunity 'at a very early age (<3 year)' while Table 1 gives LN diagnosis at 3 years for both; P2 is said to be 'without any autoantibodies' initially while Table 3 lists 'Other autoantibodies' as 'Negative' alongside positive ANA and dsDNA (read as other antibodies negative, not a contradiction).
